main_body: Flat desert sand ground patch (4x3 tiles) with scattered darker and lighter speckles and short light dashes. It is not a standing object.
top_band: none. The column scan shows only a repeating sand speckle pattern (L=182 base with 156, 204 and 125 dots), with no top band and no front face.
evidence: This is a terrain ground tile, so the 3/4 standing-object contract (top band plus front face) does not apply. The surface is a flat, seamless sand texture with no receding side faces and no elevation-style object body. Nothing in it fails the contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile, and the paving reference has 7 colours and a median of 7. The sand uses one base tone with sparse dots and a few short light dashes, so it has about 4 lightness steps against roughly 5-6 for Beodeul. The speckle layout repeats identically in every 16px tile, so the 4x3 patch looks mechanically tiled. There are no flat 5x5 fills and no outline, so the problems are low density, shallow ramps and obvious repetition. Next to the rich grass it looks thinner and flatter.
